additions.text: A lifeguard talks with Diego on the beach.
Hi! Are you swimming today?
Yes. Is the water cold?
No, it is warm. But there is a yellow flag. There are big waves.
Then I swim close, with my sister.
Very good. And use sunscreen.
Where are they?
How is the water?
What color is the flag?
Who does Diego swim with?
Do you swim in the sea?
Do you like cold or warm water?
Who do you go to the beach with?
waves
flag

Carlos looks for the right subway and asks Ana.
Excuse me, does this subway go to the park?
No, this one goes south. Your subway is the green one.
The green one? Where is it?
Over there, on the right. It is fast. Ten minutes.
Thank you very much!
Where is Carlos going?
Which subway does he need?
Where is his subway?

Do you take the subway?
Is there a park near your house?
Do you ask when you don’t know the way?

fast

Hi. I want two tacos, please.

One chicken and one beef. Are they spicy?

It is eight dollars.

Hello, Austin! My name is Lupe. I am from Guatemala and I live in Texas.
Today I sing three songs: one in English and two in Spanish.

Good morning! There is mango, pineapple and papaya.
Is the pineapple sweet?
Yes, very sweet. It is from a farm on the island.
Then, one pineapple and two mangoes.
That is six dollars. And a flower necklace as a gift!
Where are they?

Martín and Camila walk through a snowy town.
It is so cold! There is a lot of snow.
Yes, today it is minus ten degrees. Do you have gloves?
No. I have a hat, but I don’t have gloves.
There are gloves at Hank’s shop. It is over there, next to the café.
Perfect! First gloves and then hot chocolate.
What is the weather like?
What doesn’t Martín have?

What does Martín have afterwards?

Do you drink hot chocolate?

Venice Beach
roller-skating teacher
It is Venice Beach. There is sun, palm trees and lots of people. Lupita skates. She has pink skates.
Hi! I am Lupita. I teach skating. Do you skate?
Lupita gives you some skates. What do you do?
I put on the skates.
You take three steps… and you fall! Lupita laughs and helps you.
No, thanks. I watch.
Lupita dances on her skates. She skates so well!
I prefer the bike.
Lupita says: “They rent bikes over there.” She points to a shop.
A man with a big snake walks by! What do you say?
Can you skate?
Yes, I can skate. / No, I can’t. / A little.
Can you swim?
Can you ride a bike?
Do you do sports?
Yes, I play soccer. / I run. / No, I don’t do sports.
When?
With whom?
Is it hot in your city?
Yes, it is very hot. / No, it is cold.
Is it sunny today?
Do you prefer heat or cold?
Are you afraid of big animals?
Yes, I am afraid. / No, I like them.
And snakes?
What animal do you have at home?

The Venice Beach boardwalk on a Sunday. There are musicians, artists, people lifting weights outdoors and skaters who dance. Lupita teaches skating here every weekend.
My parents are from Guadalajara, but I was born here, in Los Angeles. I learned to skate at forty, imagine that! It’s never too late. What do you want to learn?
Lupita offers you a free class right now. It’s very hot. What do you answer?
Yes! But with a helmet and knee pads.
Lupita claps: “That’s what I like. Safety first.”
Better tomorrow morning, when it’s cooler.
“Perfect. At eight there’s nobody here and the sea is beautiful.”
I’d rather watch the skaters dancing.
Lupita puts on music and dances for you. People form a circle.
A guy offers you “a photo with a movie star” for ten dollars. The “star” is wearing a very strange wig.
Lupita learned to skate at forty. What do you want to learn this year?
This year I want to learn to… because…
Where can you learn it?
Is it expensive?
What do you usually do on Sundays?
On Sundays I usually… and then…
Do you go out or stay home?
Do you eat with your family?
Do you prefer doing sports alone or in a group?
I prefer… because it’s more… / I like…
What sport do you watch on TV?
Do you go to the gym?
Are there places with street artists in your city? What are they like?
Yes, in… there are… / No, in my city there aren’t…
Do you give money to the artists?
Do you take photos with them?

the helmet
the knee pads
to lift weights
to be born
the wig
Lupita is sitting on a bench with an ice pack on her ankle. She fell while teaching a class. Her students left and she looks at the sea, worried: without classes she doesn’t earn money.
Twenty years without falling and today, in front of everyone, boom! The worst part isn’t the pain, it’s the embarrassment. Has something like that ever happened to you, in front of a lot of people?
Lupita has a class with ten children in an hour. What do you tell her?
To cancel and go to the doctor now.
Lupita sighs and texts the parents. One mother replies: “Get well soon! The kids made you a drawing.”
To teach the class sitting down, explaining with her voice.
Lupita hesitates: “And what if a kid falls and I can’t help him?”
To ask another skater for help.
She calls her friend Dee, who arrives in ten minutes with her music and her energy.
A man comes over: he filmed the fall and the video already has thousands of views. He wants to know if Lupita wants to appear on a TV show.
Has something embarrassing happened to you in front of a lot of people? How did you react?
Once, at…, I… Everyone… and I…
Do you laugh about it today?
Did anyone help you?
Have you ever had an injury? How did it happen and how long did it take you to recover?
I broke / I twisted… when… It took me… to…
What was the hardest part?
Did you go back to that activity?
Compare a job with fixed hours and a job like Lupita’s.
A fixed job is more… but Lupita’s is more… The bad thing is that…
Which do you prefer?
What happens if you get sick in each one?
Have you ever seen a viral video of someone falling? What did you think of it?
Yes, I saw one where… I thought it was… because…
Did you laugh?
Would you like to go viral? Why?

embarrassment
the fall

More and more content creators film on the boardwalk. Some film people without asking permission, even children or people experiencing homelessness. Lupita and other boardwalk workers want to ask the city for a rule.

I make a living from people seeing me, that’s true. But performing in a public place isn’t the same as being the backdrop of someone else’s video. Where is the line between public and private on the street?
You have to help draft the proposal. Which rule do you propose?
Ask permission before filming any recognizable person.
A creator protests: “Then nobody could film anything on a crowded street.”
Freedom to film, but no monetizing videos with minors or vulnerable people.
Lupita nods. A lawyer in the audience asks who decides who is “vulnerable.”
Marked zones: filming allowed here, not there.
The street performers look at each other: they all want to be in the zone with cameras.
In the middle of the meeting, someone shows a video of Lupita dancing that has millions of views. She never gave permission, but thanks to that video her classes are full.
Should it be mandatory to ask permission to film someone in a public space? Why?
I think so / not, because… However, you’d have to distinguish between…
And in the case of an accident or an injustice?
What does the law say in your country?
Is Lupita inconsistent if she complains about videos but benefits from one? How would you resolve it?
I don’t think it’s inconsistent because… / Yes, a bit, since…
Can you be against something that helps you?
What would you do with that video?
If someone filmed you without permission and the video went viral, what would you do?
If it happened to me, first I would… and then… It would depend on whether…
Would you ask for money?
And if the video made you look bad?
Do social media make life in public spaces better or worse?
On the one hand… On the other… In my opinion, overall…
Are there places that were ruined by becoming famous on social media?
Do you film in public places?

the backdrop, the set

a minor

The food truck
taco truck owner
It is a food truck. Don Rigo sells tacos. It smells very good. There is a line of people.
Hello! Are you hungry? There are beef, chicken and vegetable tacos.
Which tacos do you order?
Two chicken tacos, please.
Don Rigo says: “Very good choice!”
Vegetable tacos, please.
The tacos are green, red and yellow. How pretty!
One of each.
Three tacos! Don Rigo laughs: “You are very hungry!”
The salsa is very spicy! Your face is red. What do you say?
Do you like spicy food?
Yes, I like it a lot. / No, I don’t like it. / A little.
Do you eat chili?
Do you drink water or milk with spicy food?
What do you eat in the street?
I eat… / I don’t eat in the street.
Is it cheap?
Do you eat standing up or sitting down?
Do you eat meat?
Yes, I eat meat. / No, I am vegetarian.
Do you eat fish?
What vegetables do you like?
What time do you eat lunch?
I eat at one. / I eat at three.
Do you eat at home or out?
Do you cook?
the truck
the line
the chicken
the vegetables
spicy
to be hungry
Noon on a street in East Los Angeles. Don Rigo’s truck is always on the same corner. He cooks, his daughter Ana takes the money and the radio plays rancheras.
I’ve been on this corner for twenty years. The customers are like my family: I know what each one orders. You’re new, right? What can I get you?
Don Rigo asks you: “With everything?” You don’t know what “everything” is. What do you answer?
Yes, with everything. I’ll take the risk!
Onion, cilantro, green salsa and lime. It’s delicious… and pretty spicy.
Sorry, what’s “everything”?
Ana patiently explains and lets you taste each salsa with a spoon.
No salsa, please. I don’t eat spicy food.
Don Rigo makes a sad face, but smiles: “Next time, just a little.”
The truck’s engine dies and the griddle goes cold. There are fifteen people in line. Don Rigo looks at you: “Do you know anything about engines?”
Do you have a place where they know you and what you’re going to order?
Yes, at… I always order… / No, I change places a lot.
Since when have you been going?
Why do you like it?
Which typical food from your country do you recommend to a tourist?
I recommend… It’s… and it has…
Do you know how to make it?
When is it eaten?
Don Rigo works with his daughter. Would you like to work with your family?
Yes, I’d like to because… / No, I’d rather not, because…
Who in your family would you work with?
Who would be the boss?
What music do you listen to when you cook or work?
I listen to… / I don’t listen to music, I prefer silence.
Do you sing?
What song puts you in a good mood?
the corner
to charge, to take the money
with everything
the onion
the griddle
the engine
Today there’s a health inspection. An inspector goes through the truck with a checklist. Don Rigo is nervous: in twenty years he never had a problem, but this morning the fridge broke.

When I started, I cooked at home and sold tacos on a little table, without a permit. Once the police took everything from me. I cried that night, but the next day I came back. Have you ever started something from scratch?
The inspector asks about the temperature of the meat. Don Rigo looks at you. What do you advise him?
Tell the truth about the fridge and throw away the meat.
The inspector writes it down, but thanks him for his honesty. Today he’ll only sell vegetable tacos.
Show the ice he bought in the morning.
The inspector measures the temperature: it’s right at the limit. She gives him a warning.
Close today and fix the fridge.
The customers complain, but Ana puts up a sign: “Tomorrow, free tacos for the first ten.”
The inspector finishes, puts away her checklist and asks, smiling: “Can I get three al pastor to go? My mother is from Puebla.”
Have you ever started something from scratch? What was the hardest part at first?
Yes, when I started to… At first… Later…
Who helped you?
Did you think about giving up?
What’s the best street food you’ve ever tried? Where was it?
The best was… in… It was… and it had…
How much did it cost?
Did you go back?
Have you ever told the truth even though it hurt you? What happened?
Once… and even though I could lie, I said that… In the end…
Do you regret it?
When is it better not to tell the whole truth?
Compare eating at a food truck and at a restaurant.
At a truck it’s more… but at a restaurant… I prefer…
Where did you last eat out?
Are there food trucks in your city?
the health inspection
the fridge
the permit
from scratch
to go, takeout
to give up
Ana wants to change the menu: vegan tacos, app orders and a second truck in an office district. Don Rigo says his mother’s recipe is not to be touched. Tonight they’re arguing in the truck’s kitchen.

My daughter studied business and she has good ideas, I’m not saying she doesn’t. But if everything changes, what’s left of us? People come for the same old flavor. Can you grow without losing what makes you special?
They both ask you to decide on the first change. Which one do you choose?
Add a vegan taco, but keep the original recipe intact.
Don Rigo grumbles… and asks what goes into a vegan taco “that’s worth it.”
Try the app for three months and measure whether new customers come.
Ana already has a spreadsheet ready. Her father looks at her with a mix of pride and fear.
No changes until Ana learns all her grandmother’s recipes.
Ana crosses her arms: “I’ve known them since I was twelve, Dad.”
A lifelong customer arrives with news: they’re going to build a train station on that corner and the truck will have to move in six months, like it or not.
Can you grow without losing your essence? Give an example of a company, a place or a person.
I think so / not. For example,… started… and now…
What do those who succeed have in common?
Did you like something better before it became famous?
In a family business, who should have the final say: the generation that created it or the one that will carry it on?
The way I see it… because… Ideally…
Do you know a family business that changed hands?
Would you work for your parents?
If you had to move your life or your work because of something you can’t control, how would you face it?
First I’d try to… Then… I think the hardest part would be…
Has something similar happened to you?
Is it better to resist or adapt?
Should traditional recipes change with the times (vegan, gluten-free…) or is it better to respect them as they are?
It depends on… On the one hand,… but on the other,…
Which dish from your country should nobody change?
Have you tried a modern version of a classic dish?
the family business
the recipe
the order
to grumble
the spreadsheet
to face, to deal with
The creative studio
animator
It is a drawing studio. There are computers, papers and colors. Ellie draws characters for movies.
Hi! I am Ellie. I draw characters. Look: it is a blue cat. Do you draw?
Ellie says: “What color is the cat?” What do you say?
It is green.
Ellie paints the cat green. It is very funny!
It is black and white.
Ellie says: “Elegant!”
It is many colors.
Now the cat is a rainbow. Ellie claps.
The computer turns off! The drawing is gone. What do you say?
Do you draw well?
Yes, I draw well. / No, I draw badly. / A little.
What do you draw?
With a pencil or a computer?
What is your favorite movie?
My favorite movie is…
Is it animated?
Do you watch movies at home or at the movie theater?
Do you use the computer every day?
Yes, I use the computer every day. / No, I use my phone.
How many hours?
For work or for fun?
What animal do you draw?
I draw a dog / a bird / a fish.
Is it big or small?
What is its name?
to draw
the character
the computer
the movie
the color
to turn off
An animation studio in Burbank, near the big film studios. There are whiteboards full of sketches, clay figures and cold coffee on every desk. Ellie is working on a children’s series.
We have a problem today: the main character has no name. She’s a turtle who wants to be a firefighter. What would you call her?
Ellie needs to decide the turtle’s color before five. What do you suggest?
Classic green, like real turtles.
“Safe and easy,” says Ellie. “But it doesn’t stand out much…”
Red, like a fire truck.
Ellie paints her in a minute. The whole team says “ooooh!”
Let the kids vote.
Ellie video-calls her niece. The girl shouts: “Purple with stars!”
The director walks in with news: the channel wants the turtle to speak Spanish too. Ellie looks at you: “Would you voice her?”
What would you call a turtle who wants to be a firefighter? Why?
I’d call her… because she’s…
What other animal would make a good firefighter?
What did you want to be as a child?
What cartoons did you watch as a child?
I used to watch… I liked it because…
Who was your favorite character?
Do you still watch them?
Do you work better in the morning or at night? And with coffee?
I work better in the… because… I drink… coffees a day.
What’s your desk like?
Do you work with music?
Is having a creative job important to you?
Yes, because… / Not much, for me it’s more important…
What creative things do you do in your free time?
Do you know someone with a creative job?
the animation studio
the sketch
modeling clay
the firefighter (woman)
to stand out
to dub, to voice
It’s eleven at night. Ellie is still at the studio. Tomorrow at nine they present the first episode to a big channel and the last scene still isn’t finished. The rest of the team has already left.
I’ve been here fourteen hours. When I was a student, a sleepless night was an adventure. Now my back hurts just thinking about it. Have you ever worked or studied all night?
Ellie has three hours of work left. What do you advise her?
To sleep four hours and finish at five in the morning.
Ellie sets three alarms. “If I don’t wake up, it’s your fault,” she says, laughing.
To present the scene unfinished and explain.
Ellie thinks about it: “At my first job I did that and it went well… I think.”
To call a coworker to help her.
Marcus answers half asleep, but in twenty minutes he’s there with two coffees.
The computer restarts to update. Ellie didn’t save the last forty minutes of work.
Have you ever worked or studied all night? Was it worth it?
Yes, once before… I stayed up until… and the next day…
What did you have to stay awake?
Would you do it again?
Have you ever lost important work on the computer? What did you do?
Yes, once my… got deleted and I had to…
Do you make backups now?
How did you react?
Compare how you used to work when you were younger and how you work now.
Before I used to… but now… Now I’m more… and less…
What good habit do you have now?
What do you miss from before?
Do you ask for help easily when you’re running late, or do you prefer to do everything yourself?
Usually I… because… The last time I asked for help…
Who do you call in an emergency?
Do you find it hard to delegate?
the episode
the scene
the back
to save (a file)
the backup
to be worth it
The studio is in crisis: a company offers to make the series’ backgrounds with artificial intelligence in a week and for a fraction of the price. Ellie leads the background team: six people.

I’m not an enemy of technology: I’ve been drawing on a computer for fifteen years. But those machines learned by looking at the work of artists who never gave permission. And my team has mortgages. Where would you draw the line?
The director asks you for an outside opinion before deciding. What do you recommend?
Use the tool, but only as a draft, and have the team make the final version.
Ellie considers it. A colleague asks: “And how long until they say the draft is good enough?”
Don’t use it and promote that as a value of the series: “handmade.”
The director smiles: “Lovely… and who pays the difference?”
Use it only if the company proves it paid the artists whose work it trained on.
The company doesn’t answer that question. That silence says a lot.
One of the youngest members of the team confesses he already uses those tools at home to practice, and that without them he wouldn’t have gotten this job.
Which creative jobs do you think artificial intelligence can do well, and which shouldn’t it do?
I think it can… but it shouldn’t… because…
Would you notice the difference in a movie?
Would you pay more for something handmade?
If a cheaper machine could do your job, what arguments would you use to defend it?
I’d argue that… Besides, a machine can’t…
Would you learn to use that machine?
Which part of your job would you like to automate?
Is it fair for a tool to learn from artists’ work without paying them? How should it be regulated?
I think it’s… There should be a law that… so that…
Is it different from a student who copies a master?
Who is the author of an image made with AI?
What would you say to the young colleague? Is he right about anything?
I’d tell him that… He’s right that…, but…
Do new generations see technology differently?
Do you use tools like that? What for?
the backgrounds
the mortgage
the draft
handmade
to train (a model)
to regulate
The residential street
retired neighbor
It is a street with low houses. There are gardens and cars. Don Ernesto waters his plants. He is old and kind.
Good morning! I am Ernesto. This is my house. Where do you live?
Don Ernesto has a lot of lemons. What do you say?
Can I have a lemon, please?
He gives you five lemons. “For lemonade!”
What a pretty tree!
Don Ernesto smiles: “It is forty years old.”
I don’t like lemons.
Don Ernesto laughs: “And oranges?”
The water comes out very strong and gets you wet! What do you say?
Do you live in a house or an apartment?
I live in a house. / I live in an apartment.
Is it big or small?
Does it have a garden?
Do you have plants or trees?
I have… plants. / I don’t have any.
Do you water your plants?
What is your favorite flower?
Do you know your neighbors?
Yes, I know… / No, I don’t know them.
Are they nice?
Do you talk to them?
What fruit do you like?
I like oranges / apples…
Do you drink juice?
Do you eat fruit every day?
the house
the garden, the yard
to water
the lemon
the neighbor
to get wet
A quiet street in the San Fernando Valley. One-story houses, mailboxes on the sidewalk and dry mountains in the background. Don Ernesto has lived here since 1979. Today he’s painting his fence white.
I used to know all the neighbors. Now they change every two years and we hardly talk. That’s why I say hello to everyone. Do you talk to your neighbors?
Don Ernesto offers you a brush: “Will you help me for ten minutes?” What do you do?
Sure. Where do I start?
You paint a piece of the fence. Don Ernesto tells you the story of every house on the street.
Sorry, I’m in a hurry.
“No problem. I’ll be here tomorrow… and the day after,” he says with a smile.
I offer him a lemonade in exchange for a story.
You sit on the porch. He tells you how he arrived from Sonora at twenty.
The neighbor across the street runs out: her cat climbed onto the roof and can’t get down. Don Ernesto is already looking for the ladder.
How long have you been living in your home? Do you like your street?
I’ve lived there since… I like it because… / I don’t like it because…
What is nearby?
Is it quiet or noisy?
Do you help your neighbors? Do they help you?
Yes, sometimes I help them with… / Not much, because…
Do you borrow things from them: salt, tools…?
Do you have a neighbor’s key?
Do you prefer living downtown or in a quiet neighborhood?
I prefer… because… but…
Do you need a car where you live?
Where are you going to live in ten years?
Which household chores do you like and which don’t you?
I like… but I don’t like… at all
Can you paint a wall?
Who does the most chores in your home?
the fence
the mailbox
the sidewalk
the paintbrush
the porch
the ladder
There’s a drought in California and the city is limiting garden watering to two days a week. Don Ernesto’s lawn, which was always the greenest on the street, is turning yellow.

My wife planted this lawn the year we got married. She died three years ago and every morning I water it thinking of her. Now they tell me I can’t. I understand the law… but it’s hard for me. Have you ever had to change a habit you really loved?
Don Ernesto asks for your advice. What do you suggest?
Replace the lawn with desert plants, and dedicate a special corner to his wife.
He goes quiet. Then he says: “She liked cactus flowers… I never thought of that.”
Collect shower water in buckets for watering.
Don Ernesto laughs: “My wife used to do that in Sonora, when we were poor.”
Leave the lawn yellow: it’s beautiful in its own way too.
“Yellow like her hair when she was young,” he says, and almost smiles.
A new neighbor waters his yard every day in secret, at night. Don Ernesto saw him yesterday. He doesn’t know whether to say something, report him or keep quiet.
Have you ever had to change a habit you really loved? Why?
Yes, I always used to… but I had to stop because…
Do you miss it?
Did you replace it with another one?
Were there ever water problems, extreme heat or cold where you lived? What did people do?
Yes, in… there was… People… and we…
Did anything change afterward?
Are you careful with water at home?
What would you do about the neighbor who waters in secret?
I’d talk to him / I wouldn’t say anything / I’d report him because…
Have you ever reported someone?
Is it different if it’s an older person or a rich neighbor?
Compare a neighborhood where everyone knows each other with one where nobody does.
Where everyone knows each other there’s more… but also… On the other hand…
Which one did you grow up in?
Which do you prefer now?
the drought
watering, irrigation
the lawn
in secret
to report (to the authorities)
the habit, the custom

A real estate company offers Don Ernesto more than a million dollars for his house: they want to tear it down and build four apartments. The neighbors are divided: some want the street to stay the same, others say the city needs housing.

My grandchildren can’t afford rent here. If I sell, I can help all of them with that money. But my children grew up in this house, and the street would change forever. What weighs more: memory or the future?
